To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the pair JTransformer and CTC is the most promising infrastructure, (2) JDT and CTC can be used to detect patterns in a few seconds, and (3) JDT and JTransformer are complementary.
logic code analysis and manipulation frameworks provide an excellent infrastructure for concern detection and transformation.
the pair JDT + CTC is a suitable infrastructure for concern detection and that the use of design patterns as concerns is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general framework for the analysis and transformation of large software systems that is based on the combination of a logic programming language with a code transformation engine.
a systematic evaluation of the potential of logic code analysis and code transformation frameworks as general infrastructures for concern extraction and transformation.
the following question: How to detect and extract concerns efficiently in large software systems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best infrastructure is the one that fits best to the application at hand.

the best choice of infrastructure depends on a number of factors, such as the nature and size of the software system to be analyzed, the desired precision and recall of a detection, the desired performance, and the desired expressiveness of the detection.

there is no single best infrastructure, but rather a number of different infrastructures that are suitable for different tasks, and that the choice of the best one depends on the particular task at hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of JTransformer & CDT and CTC & JastAdd seems most promising for a fast, scalable, and precise detection and extraction of concerns.
the combination of JTransformer and CTC is the best choice for a general-purpose concern detection and extraction infrastructure.
the use of logic-based frameworks as infrastructures for concern extraction is a promising avenue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of declarative specifications, such as those provided by logic programming languages, is an important factor for the success of such infrastructures.
logic-based infrastructures can be used to detect concerns with very high precision in mere seconds even for large software systems.
logic-based frameworks provide a good basis for the development of fast concern detectors.
